sents.text: One mistake is so common it gets its own slide: sudo pip install.
It installs packages into the system's own Python, which the operating system itself depends on, and it can break it.
Instead, activate your project's virtual environment and run pip without sudo.
Because sudo removes the safety net, read the whole command before you press Enter.
Only paste commands from sources you trust.
Be very wary of anything that downloads a script from the internet and pipes it straight into sudo bash.
And check every path twice, especially with rm dash r.
rm dash r, tilde slash old project, deletes one folder.
Add a single space after the slash, and the same command deletes your entire home folder, and then anything called old project.
Linux does exactly what you type, not what you meant.
Remember that whoami in Colab answered root?
Colab gives you a throwaway machine, so it runs you as root, and you don't need sudo there.
That makes it a safe place to practise.
On real servers and on your own laptop, you'll be a normal user, and sudo is how you ask for more.
